# Bring Backend Comments in Line with the Comment Rules (#1171) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Close #1171 in 23 PRs. PR A adds a PHPStan guard that caps every comment block at three lines of prose, with an allow-list of the files still waiting for their sweep. PRs B–W then sweep the backend module by module. Each sweep deletes its own group from the allow-list, so the guard proves that PR's sweep. After PR W the whole tree is checked and the allow-list is gone. #1171 runs only after #1169 and #1172 have closed. The waves below fix the merge order only: B–N come first, O–S follow them (they sweep files #1169 E–G edited), and T–W come last (files #1169 H edited). Per PR: its tasks, what it changes (files and blocks, measured at the SHA its part was written at: B–N `021f9ec1`, O–S `fba354b5`, T–W `0863e373`), and what its X0 positive control expects (its row of PR A's seed table; the ≈ figure is re-measured at `fb46acb5`, where #1172 closed: every row equals its `021f9ec1` value).

**Architecture:**
- **One guard, one ratchet.** `CommentBlockLengthRule` reports every comment block with more than three lines of prose, on the block's first line. What a block is and what counts as prose follow the counting rules in the "Disposition rubric" section: PHPDoc types, tool directives and delimiter lines are not prose, and comment tokens with only whitespace between them are one block. `UnsweptCommentFiles::FILES` holds exact file paths relative to `backend/`, grouped by PR letter under a one-line `// B` marker. PR A generates it from the tree it lands on. Every file not on the list is checked from day one, new files included. Each sweep PR deletes exactly its own group in the same PR, and that is its proof: the guard count for the group was N before the sweep and is 0 after it. PR W deletes the class and the constructor parameter.
- **The rubric is binding.** Every block in a listed file is judged, not only the flagged ones. Apply the steps in this order: delete (narration, history, review citations, restated signatures, copied paragraphs, banners, stale pointers); replace with code only when small and behaviour-preserving; shorten to one line (three at most) when a future reader would get the code wrong without it; move to `docs/` only current reasoning that cannot fit; keep. Security invariants keep a short warning in the code. The full text is in "Disposition rubric" below, copied verbatim from the scope report, which is not in the repository.
- **Docs anchors.** `docs/security.md` is created by PR B with exactly this header, and later PRs append `## <Title>` sections:
  ```
  # Security invariants

  One section per invariant the backend relies on. A code comment that points here names the section's anchor.
  ```
  Code comments point by anchor, never by section number: `docs/security.md#login-timing`, `docs/oauth-sign-in.md#the-id-token-trust-boundary`. A section added to an existing doc gives its full text and the heading it goes under.
- **Comment-only by default.** A rename, extraction or constant that replaces a comment is allowed only when it is small and behaviour-preserving, and the plan names the test that covers it. Anything larger, and every "missing enforcement" a comment describes, goes to the PR's "Final-report items", not into code.

**Tech Stack:** PHP 8.4, Symfony 7.4, PHPStan 2.2 (`Rule<FileNode>`, `RuleTestCase`, the JSON error format), PHP's tokenizer (`PhpToken::tokenize()`), PHPUnit 12, PHP_CodeSniffer (PSR-12), PHPMD codesize, phptramp, Infection, jq.

**Spec:**
- GitHub issue #1171 (`gh issue view 1171`).
- CLAUDE.md, "PHP code style — Clean Code is mandatory": "Default to no comment, and mean it", "One line. Three at the absolute most", "Delete on sight"; the OIDC boundary note (`IdTokenModel` and friends and `OidcBoundaryTest` stay).
- The planner's scope report for #1171 (measured at `021f9ec1`, outside the repository). Its binding parts are copied here: the rubric, the PR table and the carry-forward items.
- The #1169 plan, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-29-1169-final-readonly-injection.md`, for the process conventions this plan repeats.

## What the guard measures at `021f9ec1`

This plan's classifier was measured over the tree at `021f9ec1`, using a port of the code in Task A1 run outside the repository. With the list empty, it reports **1,789 blocks in 792 files** (916 `src`, 873 `tests`). The scope's scripts counted 1,787 blocks in 791 files. The difference comes from counting rules the scope defined but its scripts did not implement: the blank-line join, a `//` run joining the docblock below it, directive reasons counted as prose, and `@template … of`, `@phpstan-import-type` and `@method` signatures counted as type. ## Disposition rubric

Copied verbatim from the scope report (§4.1–§4.3). The planner's anchor ruling below it replaces the `§N` pointer form.

### 4.1 Per block, in this order

1. **Delete** when the block only: narrates history, a review or a fix round ("used to", "an earlier version of this
   comment", "fix round 1", "REVIEWER NOTE", "#311 final review, Critical 2", "replaces a longer history of…"); explains
   code by the tool that forced it (phptramp, PHPMD, PHPStan, "NOT final readonly") where the code, an attribute
   (`#[ProcessLifetimeState]`), or the gate itself already says it; restates the next line, the class name or the
   signature (§1.5); repeats a docblock copied elsewhere (the ROLE_ADMIN paragraph ×9; `security.yaml` is its home);
   is a banner (split or rename instead); or points at a path/method that moved (fix the reference if the pointer is
   the whole point, else delete).
2. **Replace with code** when a name, constant, extracted method or typed value would carry it (CLAUDE.md's first
   choice) — only when behaviour-preserving and small; list it in the plan with the test that covers it (§4.3).
3. **Shorten to one line** (three at most) when a future reader would get the code *wrong* without it: a non-obvious
   invariant, a hard-won bug, a security property. State the *what must stay true*, not the story.
4. **Move to docs/** only the part a maintainer needs that cannot fit in three lines *and* is current (a threat
   model, a sizing argument). Leave a ≤ 3-line comment with the invariant plus `docs/<file>.md §N`. History never moves
   to docs — it is in git and the issue.
5. **Keep** a block of ≤ 3 prose lines that passes 1–2.

`#NNN` references: delete when the comment goes, or when the reference only dates the code ("since #444", "(#720)"
after a sentence that stands alone). Keep it when the kept sentence rests on evidence recorded in that issue (a
measurement, a reproduction) that the reader may need to re-check.

Docs targets:

| Content | Target |
|---|---|
| OAuth flow binding, login-code binding, the accepted redemption race (LoginCodeStore, OAuthStateStore) | `docs/oauth-sign-in.md` §4.2 "Why there is a cookie at all: login CSRF" (extend) |
| CORS policy, why a listener not nelmio | `docs/oauth-sign-in.md` §4.3 "`APP_FRONTEND_URL` is the CORS origin" (extend) |
| OIDC trust boundary (IdTokenModel, IdTokenVerifier's "why the signature is not verified here", TokenEndpoint) | `docs/oauth-sign-in.md` §8 (developer) — new §8.7 "The ID-token trust boundary" |
| JWT/password invalidation, passkey firewall, login timing equalizer, login rate-limit normalization, insecure-config guard | new `docs/security.md`, one section per invariant (created by B, extended by C) |
| Run lock TTL sizing and keepalive, worker presence window, poll/worker arbitration | `docs/recommendations-runs.md`, new "For developers" section (as `backup.md` §8), and `docs/for-you-scheduling.md` "With the background worker" for the presence window |

### 4.2 The security-invariant exception

Security-invariant prose — the OIDC boundary, `UserIdentityRepository`'s two-column lookup, `UserIdentity`'s
collation, the JWT `iat` comparison, the login-code browser binding — **keeps a short warning in the code**, because a
future reader who "simplifies" it opens a hole. The warning is ≤ 3 lines and says what must not change and what breaks
if it does; the threat model and history go to docs / the commit. The OIDC boundary *code* (`IdTokenModel` and
friends) and `OidcBoundaryTest` are not touched (CLAUDE.md).

### 4.3 Scope discipline

- Default: comment-only diffs. A rename/extract/constant that replaces a comment is allowed when behaviour-preserving,
  listed in the plan with its covering test, and small; anything larger goes to the final report.
- A block that documents a *missing enforcement* (PasskeyController's "nothing enforces the list… fails open") is a
  test or rule waiting to be written: shorten the comment and record the enforcement idea in the final report — do
  not build it in a sweep PR.

**Anchor ruling (planner, binding; replaces the `§N` form in step 4 and the table above).** A comment names a docs anchor, never a section number: `docs/oauth-sign-in.md#the-id-token-trust-boundary`, `docs/security.md#login-timing`. The docs targets in the table stay the same. Only the way a comment points at them changes.

## Planner rulings (binding for every PR)

1. **The guard** is `CommentBlockLengthRule` with the exact-path allow-list `tests/PhpStan/UnsweptCommentFiles.php`. PR A adds both, each sweep PR deletes its group, and PR W deletes the list.
2. **#1171 executes after #1169 and #1172 have closed.** Each PR re-reads its files at its starting SHA; every edit quotes the complete text it replaces, and line numbers are anchors only. PR A seeds from the tree it lands on, with no extra paths for files #1169 moved.
3. **Docs** follow the anchor ruling above. PR B creates `docs/security.md`; later PRs only append.
4. **Comment-only by default** (see Architecture).
5. **Every block in a listed file is judged**, not only the flagged ones. An unchanged block needs no plan entry; every changed block has one.
6. **`#NNN` references** follow the rubric: delete one that only dates the code; keep one when the kept sentence rests on evidence recorded in that issue.
7. **Restating `@param`/`@return`** that repeat the native type: delete. A tag that repeats the native type but carries a description keeps the description only if it passes the rubric; otherwise the tag goes. PHPStan-needed types (generics, `list<>`, array shapes, `@template`, `@phpstan-type`) always stay.
8. **Refs discipline:** every PR is `Refs #1171` except PR W (`Closes #1171`).
9. **Tool-explanation notes** (cross-PR ruling, made while the parts were written): a comment that only explains an `@lang TEXT` directive or a heredoc `@noinspection` directive, and every PDepend-parentheses note, is deleted; the directive stays and the PhpStorm or PHPMD gate catches its removal. One rule for every PR, "input under test" and "do not edit this input" notes included (planner ruling at assembly); a reason written inside the directive itself (`/** @noinspection … <reason> */`) is part of the annotation and stays.
10. **Config comments have one home:** every yaml, neon, XML, `.env` and `infection.json5` comment in `backend/` is PR W's; no other PR edits one.
11. **Calibration** (from the waves): keep a `#NNN` only when the kept sentence warns against a change and rests on a measurement or reproduction recorded in that issue; publisher names only in the approved host-specific classes or where they show a URL shape the code matches; delete short restating comments even under the bar; state a rule once at its home and delete its copies, a test's copy of its class's rule included; a wrong comment is corrected, not only shortened.
12. **Anchors name headings.** "By anchor, never by section number" forbids prose pointers such as "§4" or "section 7"; it does not forbid the slug of an existing heading. An existing heading whose topic is exactly the comment's topic is a valid target, numbered or not (`docs/backup.md#4-when-a-restore-fails`). A PR adds a new heading only when no existing heading narrowly holds the topic (F5's `#### The flow cookie`).

## Global Constraints

- **Paths and commands are relative to `backend/`**, except steps marked "from the repository root", `docs/…` and `CLAUDE.md` (at the repository root).
- **Quoted text wins over line numbers.** Every edit names the complete text it replaces; line numbers are anchors only. If the quoted text is not there at your starting SHA (#1169, #1172 or a feature PR changed it), stop and report the file and the text you found. Do not guess.
- **Reconcile signal.** Each sweep PR's Task X0 deletes its group and runs **the guard count** (next item). The expected number is that letter's row in PR A's recorded seed table. A different number is a reconcile gap: report it to the planner before sweeping. Do not sweep a file that is not in the group, and do not leave a group file on the list.
- **The guard count** is the one way to count the rule's findings, from `backend/`:
  ```bash
  bin/console cache:warmup -q \
    && vendor/bin/phpstan clear-result-cache -q \
    && vendor/bin/phpstan analyse --memory-limit=512M --error-format=json 2>/dev/null \
    | jq '[.files[].messages[] | select(.identifier == "simpleFeedReader.commentBlockLength")] | length'
  ```
  PHPStan's raw format prints a message's identifier only with `-v` or under a detected agent, so a grep on the raw output counts nothing. The JSON formatter of PHPStan 2.2.5 (locked at `021f9ec1`) always emits `identifier`. `--memory-limit=512M` is the limit `composer stan` passes. Clearing the result cache makes a count after an edit to `UnsweptCommentFiles` alone deterministic. A part that calls it COUNT means this command.
- **The guard listing** names each finding as `path:line`, relative to `backend/`, right after a guard count (the cache is warm and cleared):
  ```bash
  vendor/bin/phpstan analyse --memory-limit=512M --error-format=json 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r '.files | to_entries[] | .key as $f | .value.messages[] | select(.identifier == "simpleFeedReader.commentBlockLength") | "\($f):\(.line)"' \
    | sed "s|^$PWD/||"
  ```
  Pipe it through `cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c` for per-file counts. A part's "listing command" means this one.
- **Per-task checks are cheap; the full gates run once per PR (planner ruling 13).** #1171 changes comments, so no task runs the test suite or a whole-tree gate. Every task after X0 ends, before its commit, with the same "Task check" step and nothing else: `php -l` on every changed PHP file, `vendor/bin/phpcs -q` on those files only, and `code-unchanged.php` (next item). No `php bin/phpunit` (not even filtered or on a directory), no `composer test`, no `composer stan` or `phpstan analyse`, no guard count, no `composer md`/`tramp`, no Infection and no PhpStorm lint inside a task; stale-reference greps belong to X-final. The one exception is a task whose entries change code (D1's `match`, D7's and V5's import removals, E1's `previous:`, S6's constants, W3's allow-list removal; PR A's rule and fixture tasks, whose test-first steps stay as written): it also runs its named covering test file(s), listed explicitly, never a directory, and keeps its deletion checks on that file. Subagent reviewers during tasks run nothing either; they read the diff. X0 (the positive control) stays. X-final is the full gate once per PR: `composer cs`, `cache:warmup` + `composer stan` (0 errors, 0 `commentBlockLength`), `composer md`, `composer tramp`, `rm -rf var/cache/test*` then native `php bin/phpunit`, the stale-reference greps, PhpStorm lint of the changed PHP (deleting a docblock `@var` or a `@noinspection` note can surface an inspection CI never runs), and `code-unchanged.php` against the merge-base, whose output must be exactly the `CODE CHANGED` lines of the PR's code-changing tasks, or nothing. Not locally: the MySQL leg (CI runs it), `/simplify`, and the Opus final review, which only A (adds the rule) and W (removes the allow-list) keep; a PR with a code-changing task (D, E, S, V) gets a sonnet review of those tasks' diff only, and a comments-only PR gets none. `composer infection:diff` runs locally only in a PR whose Task checks reported a `CODE CHANGED` file (A, D, E, S, V, W); in a comments-only PR, CI runs it and the local run is skipped, because deleted or rewritten comment lines give Infection nothing to mutate. The merge flow and the closing-keyword gate are unchanged. Guard break tests that parts had put inside tasks (B8, E6, K9) moved to their X-final, as did V4's claim plants and W3's whole-tree plant and PHPMD run.
- **`code-unchanged.php`** — write it once per PR to `var/comment-rules-1171/code-unchanged.php` (it is git-ignored with the rest of `var/`), from `backend/`:
  ```php
  <?php

  declare(strict_types=1);

  // One-off for #1171, never committed. From backend/: php var/comment-rules-1171/code-unchanged.php [<base>]
  // Prints each changed PHP file whose tokens, comments and whitespace aside, differ from <base> (HEAD); exits 1 if any does.
  $base = $argv[1] ?? 'HEAD';
  $ignored = ['tests/PhpStan/UnsweptCommentFiles.php'];
  $codeTokens = static function (string $source): array {
      $kept = [];
      foreach (token_get_all($source) as $token) {
          if (is_array($token) && in_array($token[0], [T_COMMENT, T_DOC_COMMENT, T_WHITESPACE], true)) {
              continue;
          }
          $kept[] = is_array($token) ? [$token[0], $token[1]] : $token;
      }

      return $kept;
  };
  exec('git diff --name-only --relative ' . escapeshellarg($base) . " -- '*.php'", $paths, $status);
  exec("git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- '*.php'", $untracked, $untrackedStatus);
  if (0 !== $status || 0 !== $untrackedStatus) {
      fwrite(STDERR, "git diff failed\n");
      exit(2);
  }
  $paths = array_values(array_unique([...$paths, ...$untracked]));
  $changed = false;
  foreach ($paths as $path) {
      if (in_array($path, $ignored, true)) {
          continue;
      }
      exec('git cat-file -e ' . escapeshellarg($base . ':./' . $path) . ' 2>/dev/null', $unused, $inHead);
      if (0 !== $inHead) {
          echo "NEW {$path}\n";
          $changed = true;
          continue;
      }
      if (!is_file($path)) {
          echo "DELETED {$path}\n";
          $changed = true;
          continue;
      }
      $old = (string) shell_exec('git show ' . escapeshellarg($base . ':./' . $path));
      if ($codeTokens($old) !== $codeTokens((string) file_get_contents($path))) {
          echo "CODE CHANGED {$path}\n";
          $changed = true;
      }
  }
  exit($changed ? 1 : 0);
  ```
  Without an argument it compares the working tree with the last commit, so it sees exactly the task's uncommitted edits; X-final passes the merge-base (`"$(git merge-base origin/develop HEAD)"`) to check the whole PR. The allow-list file is ignored: its group deletion is data, carried unstaged from X0. A file with no version at the base prints `NEW <path>`, untracked ones included (`git diff` alone never lists an untracked file; an untracked PHP file of another session's also prints `NEW`: leave it alone and name it in the report), and a deleted one `DELETED <path>`. Each Task check, and each X-final's PR-wide run, names its exact expected output: nothing for comments-only work, or the `CODE CHANGED` lines of the files the code-changing entries name.
- **The allow-list only shrinks.** A sweep PR deletes its whole group and never adds a path. If a block truly cannot shrink below four prose lines, report it to the planner. Do not add an `EXCEPTIONS` map on your own.
- **Clean Code (CLAUDE.md) is mandatory**, including in `tests/`. New or rewritten comments meet the bar they enforce: one line by default, three at most.
- **Symfony recipe files are never edited** (`public/index.php`, `bin/console`, `config/bundles.php`, `config/preload.php` and the other Flex-shipped files). They sit outside `src` and `tests`, so the rule never reads them. `src/Kernel.php` is a recipe file this project has already extended: its project-written comment in `boot()` is in scope (PR I). The recipe's own lines stay untouched.
- **PHPStan at level max:** no baseline entry, no `@phpstan-ignore` without a reason on the same line. Run `bin/console cache:warmup` before `composer stan`.
- **PHPMD:** `composer md` reads `src` only. Every touched `src` file is PHPMD-clean. New `tests/PhpStan` helpers get an explicit PHPMD run (PR A names the command).
- **PhpStorm inspections** (`mcp__phpstorm__lint_files`) on every changed PHP file: ERROR and WARNING block. A finding you did not cause must be proven pre-existing by running the same inspection on `origin/develop`.
- **Infection:** a comment-only diff produces no mutants (`--ignore-msi-with-no-mutations`). A rename or extraction produces mutants on its lines and must meet `minMsi`; an escaped mutant gets a killing test in the task that owns it, never an `ignore`.
- **Test legs:** locally, only the native leg, once per PR in X-final: `rm -rf var/cache/test*`, then `php bin/phpunit`. CI runs the MySQL leg on the PR (ruling 13); no step runs `composer test` in the container.
- **Every deletion check has a quoted FAIL.** The step names the one edit and the expected FAIL. The implementer runs every check, restores each by hand with the Edit tool (never `git checkout --`), and quotes the FAIL output in the task report. A check without a quoted FAIL is not done. In PRs A and W the Opus reviewer re-runs at least one of them and quotes that FAIL too.
- **Every grep has a positive control.** The same pattern and pathspec must print a known hit, either a planted one or one the step names. Use `git grep -E` and escape backslashes. Never use `-F` with backslashes. A plain `**` pathspec matches nothing: use `':(glob)…'` or a directory.
- **Commits:** `type(#1171): <lower-case summary>`. Use `chore` for the guard, the allow-list and code-comment sweeps, and `docs` for `docs/` and the plan copy. One commit per task unless the task says otherwise. No attribution lines.
- **Branches**, each cut from `origin/develop` after the previous PR merged: `chore/1171-comment-rules-a` through `chore/1171-comment-rules-w`, the lower-case PR letter last. PRs merge into `develop` (git-flow), never `main`.
- **PR bodies and commits of PRs A–V say `Refs #1171` and contain no close/fix/resolve keyword in any form, not even in prose or a quote.** Write "the review narration" rather than quoting "fix round". `gh pr create` runs only as the last link of the `&&` chain in "The closing-keyword gate" below. PR W's body says `Closes #1171`.
- **Merge:** watch with the Monitor tool, one command, `gh pr checks <PR> --watch --fail-fast`. When it exits 0, run `gh pr merge <PR> --merge`. Never `--auto`. Then `gh issue view 1171 --json state --jq .state`: `OPEN` after A–V, `CLOSED` after W.
- **The checkout is shared.** Run `git status --short && git branch --show-current` before any `switch`, `reset` or `stash`, and leave another session's files alone. Work in place, with no worktrees.
- **Scratch files** go to `var/comment-rules-1171/` (git-ignored with the rest of `var/`), never elsewhere in the tree.
- **Foreground only.** Every command in this plan runs in the foreground and finishes before the next starts: no background jobs, no poll loops, no `sleep` loops, and never two test legs at once. The one watcher is the Monitor tool's single `gh pr checks <PR> --watch --fail-fast` per PR ("Merge").
- **Reviews (ruling 13).** No `/simplify` run. Only PRs A and W get an Opus final review before the PR opens (one fresh reviewer subagent with `model: "opus"`, the PR's plan section, the rubric and `git diff origin/develop...HEAD`; it reports and does not fix; fix each Important-or-above finding in its own commit, `chore(#1171): review — <finding>`). A PR with a code-changing task (D, E, S, V) gets a sonnet review of those tasks' diff only. A comments-only PR gets no review; its X0 positive control, the X-final gates and the PR-wide code-unchanged check carry it.
- **Every finishing task** also scans the dev log after the suites (the "Dev log" item) and opens its PR through "The closing-keyword gate" below, with the body in `var/comment-rules-1171/pr-<x>-body.md`, whether or not its steps repeat those commands.
- **Dev log:** after the suites, scan today's log: `ls -t var/log/dev-*.log | head -1 | xargs tail -n 200 | jq -c 'select(.level >= 300)'`. Expected: nothing new.

## The closing-keyword gate

From `backend/`, with `<x>` the PR's lower-case letter, its body in `var/comment-rules-1171/pr-<x>-body.md` and its title:
```bash
KEYWORDS='(^|[^a-z])(close|closes|closed|fix|fixes|fixed|resolve|resolves|resolved)([^a-z]|$)'
printf 'this fixes it\n' | grep -iqE "$KEYWORDS" && echo 'guard control: a planted hit is seen'
printf 'fixture, prefix, resolveFor\n' | grep -iqE "$KEYWORDS" || echo 'guard control: look-alikes pass'
git push -u origin "$(git branch --show-current)"
git log origin/develop..HEAD --format=%B > var/comment-rules-1171/commits.txt
! grep -inE "$KEYWORDS" var/comment-rules-1171/commits.txt \
  && ! grep -inE "$KEYWORDS" var/comment-rules-1171/pr-<x>-body.md \
  && gh pr create --base develop --title "<title>" --body-file var/comment-rules-1171/pr-<x>-body.md
```
Expected: both control lines print, then the PR URL. A keyword in a commit or the body prints its line and stops the chain before `gh pr create`. Reword it, in an amended commit message on this unmerged branch or in the body file, and run the block again.

**Closing variant (PR W):** the body says `Closes #1171` once and nothing else closing:
```bash
! grep -inE "$KEYWORDS" var/comment-rules-1171/commits.txt \
  && grep -c '^Closes #1171' var/comment-rules-1171/pr-w-body.md \
  && ! grep -v '^Closes #1171' var/comment-rules-1171/pr-w-body.md | grep -inE "$KEYWORDS" \
  && gh pr create --base develop --title "<title>" --body-file var/comment-rules-1171/pr-w-body.md
```
Expected: `1`, then the PR URL. After creating any PR, `gh pr view --json body --jq .body | grep -inE "$KEYWORDS"` prints nothing (A–V) or only the `Closes #1171` line (W).

## Reproducing the numbers

The rule is the measurement. The scope's figures (the PR table's "actionable" and "files swept" columns) came from scripts that are not in the repository and are not needed again. Once PR A has landed:
- **Total over the bar:** the guard count.
- **Per file, for the whole tree:** in `CommentBlockLengthRule`'s constructor, temporarily replace the default `UnsweptCommentFiles::FILES` with `[]`. Run the command below, then restore the default by hand.
  ```bash
  bin/console cache:warmup -q && vendor/bin/phpstan clear-result-cache -q
  vendor/bin/phpstan analyse --memory-limit=512M --error-format=json 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg backend "$PWD/" '.files | to_entries[]
        | [(.key | ltrimstr($backend)),
           ([.value.messages[] | select(.identifier == "simpleFeedReader.commentBlockLength")] | length)]
        | select(.[1] > 0) | @tsv'
  ```
- **Per block:** the same JSON's `.line` and `.message` (the message states the prose-line count).

The rule does not measure `#NNN` references, narration words or restating tags. A sweep finds those by reading every block of its files (ruling 5).

## Assembly notes

This plan was assembled from 23 separately written parts (header + A, then B–W, each a `# PR <X>:` section). The parts were written at three SHAs: B–N at `021f9ec1`, O–S at `fba354b5`, T–W at `0863e373`. Where a part and the header disagreed, the header won. Everything below was changed at assembly; the parts' own text is otherwise unchanged.

### Unified across every part

- **Branches** are `chore/1171-comment-rules-<letter>` (B, C, D, E, F, G, H and J had `refactor/1171-…` names), cut with `git switch -c … origin/develop` (G, H, J used `git checkout -b`).
- **Commits** are `chore(#1171): …` for sweeps and the guard, `docs(#1171): …` for `docs/` and the plan copy (B–J had `refactor(#1171)`); PR titles follow. Scratch files live in `var/comment-rules-1171/` (B–F had `var/refactor-1171/`, F kept its lists as `1171-f-…` files directly under `var/` and left a scratchpad placeholder in its break test).
- **The guard count** is the header's JSON + `jq` command on the identifier `simpleFeedReader.commentBlockLength`, with the cache warm-up and result-cache clear (B–G counted with raw-format greps, some without `-v`, which count nothing; H and J skipped the warm-up, clear and memory limit). Per-file checks (C) run the same JSON filter over their files. Every "list the blocks" instruction points at the new header item "The guard listing".
- **X0** reads "the <letter> row of PR A's seed table (≈ N at <SHA>)" in all 22 sweep PRs, keeping each part's N and SHA; `composer stan`'s expected error total reads "<that number>". Ruling 13 later removed every per-task count.
- **The closing-keyword gate:** G, H and J scanned a `$BODY` variable with their own regex and passed `--body`; their PR steps now write `var/comment-rules-1171/pr-<x>-body.md` and run the header's gate. A–V say `Refs #1171`, W `Closes #1171` (W's closing variant unchanged).
- **Merge:** one Monitor per PR on `gh pr checks <PR> --watch --fail-fast`, then `gh pr merge <PR> --merge` (never `--auto`), then the issue-state check. G, H and J dropped `--repo` flags for the header's form.
- **The MySQL leg** was first unified to `docker compose exec php rm -rf var/cache/test* && docker compose exec php composer test`; ruling 13 then removed it from every local step (CI runs it).
- **Reviews:** the parts' Opus final reviews were first made a Global Constraint (PR D's writer had added one on its own); ruling 13 then dropped `/simplify` everywhere and the Opus review except in A and W, and gave D, E, S and V a sonnet review of their code-changing tasks' diff.
- **Foreground only** is a Global Constraint (the #1169 H process note).
- **Headings:** tasks are `## Task <X>n`; the finishing tasks are `<X>-final` (C12, F7 and "Finishing PR A" renamed, with their references); each PR's closing sections are "Final-report items (PR X)", "Reconcile notes (PR X)" and "Rulings made while writing PR X".
- **Header:** the Goal bullets and the Status table (197 tasks) were rebuilt from the assembled parts; the cross-PR rulings (tool-explanation notes, config comments in W, the wave calibration) became planner rulings 9–11, and the planner's anchor ruling made at assembly became ruling 12.

## Task A1: The classifier and `CommentBlockLengthRule`, test-first (not yet registered)

The rule and its helpers land unregistered, so `composer stan` stays green while they are built. A2 registers them and seeds the list.

**Files:**
- Create: `tests/PhpStan/data/comment-block-length/block-joins.php`, `prose-limit.php`, `var-one-liners.php`, `type-shapes.php`, `tool-directives.php`, `allow-listed.php`
- Create: `tests/PhpStan/CommentBlockLengthRuleTest.php`
- Create: `tests/PhpStan/CommentBlock.php`, `tests/PhpStan/PhpDocReading.php`, `tests/PhpStan/PhpDocTypeReader.php`, `tests/PhpStan/CommentProse.php`, `tests/PhpStan/CommentBlocks.php`, `tests/PhpStan/UnsweptCommentFiles.php`, `tests/PhpStan/CommentBlockLengthRule.php`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces: `App\Tests\PhpStan\CommentBlockLengthRule`, a `Rule<FileNode>` with the constructor `(CommentBlocks $commentBlocks, array $unsweptFiles = UnsweptCommentFiles::FILES)`. It reports with the identifier `simpleFeedReader.commentBlockLength` on the block's first line, with the message `This comment has <N> lines of prose; CLAUDE.md allows three at the absolute most. Rename, extract, or move the reasoning to docs/ or the commit message.`
- Produces: `CommentBlocks::in(string $code): list<CommentBlock>`; `CommentBlock` (`int $firstLine`, `int $proseLines`); `CommentProse::linesIn(list<string>): int`; `PhpDocTypeReader::reads(string $tag): bool` and `read(string $tag, string $argument): PhpDocReading`; `UnsweptCommentFiles::FILES` (empty here, seeded in A2).

**Where the helpers live, and which gates see them.** All the new classes go flat in `tests/PhpStan/`, like `ForbiddenReference`, `ServiceModuleCycle` and `ControllerEntityUse`. The rules that impose role folders and ban collaborator defaults do not cover `App\Tests\*`, so these gates do not apply to the helpers:
- `ServiceRoleRule` reads only `App\Service\` and `App\Http\` (`ServiceRoleNames::isServiceOrHttp()`) and production listeners (`isProductionNamespace()` excludes `App\Tests\`).
- `NoCollaboratorDefaultRule` reads only `App\{Command,Controller,EventListener,Http,Security,Service}\`. Even there, it flags only a default built with `new`. `UnsweptCommentFiles::FILES` is a constant array, a value.

The helpers are still plain Clean Code: `final readonly`, injected (the `ControllerEntityUse` pattern) and PHPMD-clean at the codesize ruleset (Step 7 runs PHPMD on them explicitly).

**Counting rules (what the code implements).** These restate the scope's §1.1 and §3.3 rules 1–6:
1. A block is a run of comment tokens (`/** */`, `/* */`, `//`, `#`) with only whitespace between them. That covers consecutive `//` lines, a trailing comment and the comment lines below it, blocks separated by blank lines, and a `//` run directly above a docblock.
2. Delimiter-only lines (`/**`, `*/`, `*`) are not prose.
3. A `@var` one-liner has 0 prose lines.
4. A PHPDoc type is not prose, including every line of a type whose brackets span lines. Only a description after the type (and after its `$name`) is prose. Before the type, a `@template` name and its `of` bound, a `@phpstan-type` alias name and a `@phpstan-import-type … from` clause are also not prose. So are a `@method`'s `static` keyword before the type and its `name(…)` signature after it.
5. Nothing is exempt. There are no license headers in `src` or `tests`.
6. A tool directive (`@phpstan-ignore id, id`, `phpcs:ignore Codes`, `@SuppressWarnings(…)`, `@see Symbol`, `@noinspection Name`, `@lang X`, `{@inheritDoc}`, `@codeCoverageIgnore` and the other bare markers) is not prose. Its reason text is prose, and so is phpcs's `-- reason`. Tags are read in every comment kind, so `// @phpstan-ignore arrayValues.list` counts 0.

Deliberate differences from the scope's reference script: it did not implement rules 1 (the joins) and 6 (reasons, and directives in `//` comments), and it counted `@template T of X` and `@phpstan-import-type` lines as prose. The tokenizer is PHP's own, through `PhpToken::tokenize()`: the same tokens as `token_get_all()`, but typed objects, which PHPStan level max reads without array shapes.

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Tests\PhpStan;

/** What a comment line says beyond its PHPDoc type, or how many brackets its type leaves open for the next line. */
final readonly class PhpDocReading
{
    private function __construct(public string $description, public int $openBrackets)
    {
    }

    public static function closed(string $description): self
    {
        return new self($description, 0);
    }

    public static function open(int $openBrackets): self
    {
        return new self('', $openBrackets);
    }

    public function isOpen(): bool
    {
        return $this->openBrackets > 0;
    }

    public function isProse(): bool
    {
        return !$this->isOpen() && '' !== $this->description;
    }
}
```

`tests/PhpStan/PhpDocTypeReader.php`:
```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Tests\PhpStan;

/** Reads the type off a PHPDoc tag; brackets may span lines, and `|`, `&` or `:` join a type across a space. */
final readonly class PhpDocTypeReader
{
    private const array TYPE_TAGS = [
        'param', 'param-out', 'return', 'var', 'throws', 'extends', 'implements', 'use', 'mixin', 'method',
        'property', 'property-read', 'property-write', 'template', 'template-covariant', 'template-contravariant',
        'type', 'import-type', 'assert', 'assert-if-true', 'assert-if-false', 'self-out', 'this-out',
        'require-extends', 'require-implements', 'sealed',
    ];

    private const string NOTHING = '~^~';

    private const string VARIABLE = '~^(?:\.\.\.)?&?\$\w+~';

    private const string TEMPLATE_NAME = '~^\S+\s+(?:of|as)\s+~';

    private const array BEFORE_TYPE = [
        'method' => '~^static\s+~',
        'template' => self::TEMPLATE_NAME,
        'template-covariant' => self::TEMPLATE_NAME,
        'template-contravariant' => self::TEMPLATE_NAME,
        'type' => '~^\w+\s*=?\s*~',
        'import-type' => '~^\S+\s+from\s+~',
    ];

    private const array AFTER_TYPE = [
        'param' => self::VARIABLE,
        'param-out' => self::VARIABLE,
        'var' => self::VARIABLE,
        'property' => self::VARIABLE,
        'property-read' => self::VARIABLE,
        'property-write' => self::VARIABLE,
        'assert' => self::VARIABLE,
        'assert-if-true' => self::VARIABLE,
        'assert-if-false' => self::VARIABLE,
        'method' => '~^\w+\([^)]*\)~',
        'import-type' => '~^as\s+\S+~',
    ];

    public function reads(string $tag): bool
    {
        return \in_array($tag, self::TYPE_TAGS, true);
    }

    public function read(string $tag, string $argument): PhpDocReading
    {
        $afterType = self::scan(self::textAfter(self::BEFORE_TYPE[$tag] ?? self::NOTHING, trim($argument)));
        if ($afterType->isOpen()) {
            return $afterType;
        }
        $description = self::textAfter(self::AFTER_TYPE[$tag] ?? self::NOTHING, $afterType->description);

        return PhpDocReading::closed($description);
    }

    private static function scan(string $text): PhpDocReading
    {
        $depth = 0;
        $position = 0;
        $length = strlen($text);
        while ($position < $length && !self::endsTypeAt($text, $position, $depth)) {
            $depth = self::depthAfter($text, $position, $depth);
            $position = self::afterQuoted($text, $position) + 1;
        }

        return $depth > 0 ? PhpDocReading::open($depth) : PhpDocReading::closed(trim(substr($text, $position)));
    }

    private static function endsTypeAt(string $text, int $position, int $depth): bool
    {
        return 0 === $depth && ctype_space($text[$position]) && !self::joinsAt($text, $position);
    }

    private static function joinsAt(string $text, int $position): bool
    {
        $before = substr(rtrim(substr($text, 0, $position)), -1);
        $after = substr(ltrim(substr($text, $position)), 0, 1);

        return \in_array($before, ['|', '&', ':'], true) || \in_array($after, ['|', '&'], true);
    }

    private static function depthAfter(string $text, int $position, int $depth): int
    {
        $character = $text[$position];
        if (str_contains('{<([', $character)) {
            return $depth + 1;
        }
        $isArrow = '>' === $character && $position > 0 && '-' === $text[$position - 1];
        if (str_contains('}>)]', $character) && !$isArrow) {
            return max(0, $depth - 1);
        }

        return $depth;
    }

    private static function afterQuoted(string $text, int $position): int
    {
        $quote = $text[$position];
        if ('"' !== $quote && "'" !== $quote) {
            return $position;
        }
        $closing = strpos($text, $quote, $position + 1);

        return false === $closing ? strlen($text) : $closing;
    }

    private static function textAfter(string $pattern, string $text): string
    {
        return 1 === preg_match($pattern, $text, $match) ? ltrim(substr($text, strlen($match[0]))) : $text;
    }
}
```

`tests/PhpStan/CommentProse.php`:
```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Tests\PhpStan;

/** Counts a block's prose lines: a PHPDoc type or a tool directive is not prose, a description or a reason is. */
final readonly class CommentProse
{
    private const string TAG = '~^(?:\{?@(?<tag>[\w-]+)\}?|phpcs:\w+)(?<argument>.*)$~is';

    private const string TOOL_PREFIX = '~^(?:phpstan|psalm)-~';

    private const string DIRECTIVE_ARGUMENT = '~^(?:\([^)]*\)|[^\s,]+(?:\s*,\s*[^\s,]+)*)~';

    private const array BARE_DIRECTIVES = [
        'api', 'codecoverageignore', 'codecoverageignoreend', 'codecoverageignorestart', 'deprecated', 'final',
        'immutable', 'impure', 'infection-ignore-all', 'inheritdoc', 'internal', 'pure', 'todo',
    ];

    public function __construct(private PhpDocTypeReader $types)
    {
    }

    /**
     * A type whose brackets span lines is read as one statement: only its last line can carry a description.
     *
     * @param list<string> $lines a block's lines with the comment markers stripped
     */
    public function linesIn(array $lines): int
    {
        $proseLines = 0;
        $statement = '';
        foreach ($lines as $line) {
            $statement = ltrim($statement . "\n" . $line);
            $reading = $this->read($statement);
            if ($reading->isOpen() && '' !== $line) {
                continue;
            }
            $proseLines += $reading->isProse() ? 1 : 0;
            $statement = '';
        }

        return $proseLines;
    }

    private function read(string $statement): PhpDocReading
    {
        if (1 !== preg_match(self::TAG, $statement, $match)) {
            return PhpDocReading::closed($statement);
        }
        $tag = self::textAfter(self::TOOL_PREFIX, strtolower($match['tag']));
        if ($this->types->reads($tag)) {
            return $this->types->read($tag, $match['argument']);
        }

        return PhpDocReading::closed(self::reasonAfter($tag, trim($match['argument'])));
    }

    private static function reasonAfter(string $tag, string $argument): string
    {
        $reason = \in_array($tag, self::BARE_DIRECTIVES, true)
            ? $argument
            : self::textAfter(self::DIRECTIVE_ARGUMENT, $argument);

        return trim(ltrim($reason, '-'));
    }

    private static function textAfter(string $pattern, string $text): string
    {
        return 1 === preg_match($pattern, $text, $match) ? ltrim(substr($text, strlen($match[0]))) : $text;
    }
}
```
`textAfter()` exists in two classes. That is the second occurrence, not the third, so it stays until a third caller appears.

`tests/PhpStan/CommentBlocks.php`:
```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Tests\PhpStan;

use PhpToken;

/** A file's comment blocks: comment tokens with only whitespace between them are one block. */
final readonly class CommentBlocks
{
    public function __construct(private CommentProse $prose)
    {
    }

    /** @return list<CommentBlock> */
    public function in(string $code): array
    {
        $blocks = [];
        foreach (self::commentRuns($code) as $comments) {
            $blocks[] = new CommentBlock($comments[0]->line, $this->prose->linesIn(self::textLinesOf($comments)));
        }

        return $blocks;
    }

    /** @return list<non-empty-list<PhpToken>> */
    private static function commentRuns(string $code): array
    {
        $runs = [];
        $run = [];
        foreach (PhpToken::tokenize($code) as $token) {
            if ($token->is(T_WHITESPACE)) {
                continue;
            }
            if ($token->is([T_COMMENT, T_DOC_COMMENT])) {
                $run[] = $token;
                continue;
            }
            if ([] !== $run) {
                $runs[] = $run;
            }
            $run = [];
        }

        return [] === $run ? $runs : [...$runs, $run];
    }

    /**
     * @param list<PhpToken> $comments
     *
     * @return list<string>
     */
    private static function textLinesOf(array $comments): array
    {
        $lines = [];
        foreach ($comments as $comment) {
            $strip = str_starts_with($comment->text, '/*')
                ? self::withoutBlockMarkers(...)
                : self::withoutLineMarker(...);
            $lines = [...$lines, ...array_map($strip, explode("\n", $comment->text))];
        }

        return $lines;
    }

    private static function withoutLineMarker(string $line): string
    {
        return trim(ltrim(trim($line), '/#'));
    }

    private static function withoutBlockMarkers(string $line): string
    {
        $text = trim($line);
        if (str_starts_with($text, '/*')) {
            $text = substr($text, 2);
        }
        if (str_ends_with($text, '*/')) {
            $text = substr($text, 0, -2);
        }

        return trim(ltrim(trim($text), '*'));
    }
}
```

`tests/PhpStan/CommentBlockLengthRule.php`:
```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Tests\PhpStan;

use PhpParser\Node;
use PHPStan\Analyser\Scope;
use PHPStan\Node\FileNode;
use PHPStan\Rules\IdentifierRuleError;
use PHPStan\Rules\Rule;
use PHPStan\Rules\RuleErrorBuilder;
use PHPStan\ShouldNotHappenException;

/**
 * CLAUDE.md's "one line, three at the absolute most": no comment block carries more than three lines of prose.
 *
 * @implements Rule<FileNode>
 */
final readonly class CommentBlockLengthRule implements Rule
{
    private const int MAX_PROSE_LINES = 3;

    private const string MESSAGE = 'This comment has %d lines of prose; CLAUDE.md allows three at the absolute most. '
        . 'Rename, extract, or move the reasoning to docs/ or the commit message.';

    /** @param list<string> $unsweptFiles paths relative to backend/; overridable only for the rule's own test */
    public function __construct(
        private CommentBlocks $commentBlocks,
        private array $unsweptFiles = UnsweptCommentFiles::FILES,
    ) {
    }

    public function getNodeType(): string
    {
        return FileNode::class;
    }

    public function processNode(Node $node, Scope $scope): array
    {
        $file = $scope->getFile();
        if (\in_array(self::relativePath($file), $this->unsweptFiles, true)) {
            return [];
        }

        $overlong = array_filter(
            $this->commentBlocks->in(self::contentsOf($file)),
            static fn (CommentBlock $block): bool => $block->proseLines > self::MAX_PROSE_LINES,
        );

        return array_values(array_map(self::error(...), $overlong));
    }

    private static function relativePath(string $file): string
    {
        $backend = dirname(__DIR__, 2) . '/';

        return str_starts_with($file, $backend) ? substr($file, strlen($backend)) : $file;
    }

    private static function contentsOf(string $file): string
    {
        $contents = file_get_contents($file);
        if (false === $contents) {
            throw new ShouldNotHappenException(sprintf('PHPStan analyses %s but cannot read it.', $file));
        }

        return $contents;
    }

    private static function error(CommentBlock $block): IdentifierRuleError
    {
        return RuleErrorBuilder::message(sprintf(self::MESSAGE, $block->proseLines))
            ->identifier('simpleFeedReader.commentBlockLength')
            ->line($block->firstLine)
            ->build();
    }
}
```
`ShouldNotHappenException`'s constructor is PHPStan `@api`. A file PHPStan is analysing is always readable, so the throw only guards the `string|false` type.

- [ ] **Step 1: Create `docs/security.md`** with exactly this content (later #1171 PRs append `## …` sections):

```markdown
# Security invariants

One section per invariant the backend relies on. A code comment that points here names the section's anchor.

## Insecure production config

`InsecureProductionConfigGuardListener` refuses every request in `prod` while
`ALTCHA_HMAC_KEY` still holds the placeholder committed to `.env`.

That key is the only thing that makes an ALTCHA challenge unforgeable, and the
placeholder is public: anyone holding it forges a solved proof-of-work in one
hash instead of about 150,000, so `/register` and `/password-reset-request` keep
answering `200` behind a void gate. A committed default turns a forgotten
override into a failure that looks healthy indefinitely, so the guard makes it
fail closed — the stance `MaintenanceTokenGuard` takes on an empty
`MAINTENANCE_TOKEN`.

- **It matches the exact placeholder**, not a notion of a weak key. "Not
  overridden" is a fact; a strength heuristic would miss real weak keys and
  reject fine unusual ones. `InsecureProductionConfigGuardListenerTest` reads
  `.env`, so an edited placeholder cannot silently stop matching.
- **It runs on `kernel.request`, not in a compiler pass or at kernel boot.** A
  deployment runs `cache:warmup` in `prod` before the `current` symlink flips, so
  a build-time check would abort the warmup of a misconfigured environment and
  take the whole deploy down. A host that injects the key per request (Apache
  `SetEnv`, a php-fpm pool directive) sees only the `.env` default at warmup and
  the real value at request time. Warmup, migrations and console commands are
  never refused.
- **The refusal is a `500` on every route**, not only on the two ALTCHA-gated
  ones. The exception names the variable to set and goes to the log; outside
  debug the problem document suppresses exception messages, so a client learns
  nothing. An instance that half-serves with a void CAPTCHA is quietly failing
  at what it is for.
- **`dev` and `test` are exempt**: the test suite solves real ALTCHA challenges
  with the committed key.

## OAuth account linking

`OAuthAccountLinker` decides which local account a provider-verified identity
signs in to. A wrong answer here is an account takeover, not a bug. The rules,
in the order they apply:

1. **A known identity wins.** A `user_identity` row matching (provider,
   subject) is the account, whatever address the provider reports today. A
   returning user whose provider address changed — perhaps to a victim's — stays
   on their own account.
2. **Only a linkable address links.** An address links to the account holding
   it only when the provider verified it and it is not an Apple private relay. A
   relay address is real and deliverable, but it names one (app, Apple user)
   pair rather than a person, so no login may hang on it.
3. **Otherwise a new account**, with no password, in `pending_approval` — or
   active at once when admin approval is off. The provider proved the address,
   so the account skips `pending_verification` whatever the email-confirmation
   toggle says.

Around those three:

- **An unlinkable address never becomes the login identifier.** Refusing to
  link is only half the rule: an attacker whose provider allows arbitrary
  unverified addresses could otherwise park `admin@company.example` in the
  approval queue, be approved on how the address reads, and end up sharing the
  account with the real owner once that owner recovers a password. The claimed
  address is kept on the `UserIdentity` row, visibly provider-reported.
- **Placeholder addresses.** An identity with no usable address — Apple sends
  the address only on the first authorisation — gets
  `<provider>-<first 32 hex of sha256(subject)>@oauth.invalid`. `.invalid` never
  resolves (RFC 2606), the prefix tells the admin where the account came from,
  the digest keeps the subject out of a column the admin UI shows, and the same
  identity always rebuilds the same address instead of piling up accounts.
  Approving such an account sends the welcome mail to it; that send is deferred
  to `kernel.terminate` and its failure is logged, so the bounce costs a log
  line. Every other account mail starts from an address a person typed.
- **An unverified registration is claimed.** When the address a provider just
  verified belongs to an account still in `pending_verification`, whoever set
  that account's password never proved the address. The account moves to
  `pending_approval` (or active, with approval off), its address is marked
  verified, and its password is wiped with `passwordChangedAt` stamped, which
  revokes any JWT the planter holds. The wipe happens whatever the approval
  toggle says: it is a control over an unproven credential, not a step of the
  approval workflow. Refusing to link and creating a second account instead
  would hand an attacker a cheap denial of service against the real owner and
  strand the common case, where the abandoned registration is the user's own.
  The owner gets back in by signing in with the provider again; a password
  reset works once an admin has approved the account.
- **Linking never overrules an admin.** Every status other than
  `pending_verification` is left as it is: a rejected account is not revived, a
  suspended one is not unsuspended, and an active account's password is not
  wiped, which would revoke the live sessions of a user who only signed in a
  second way. The exchange's status gate then refuses suspended and rejected
  accounts.
- **`User::$email` is never rewritten from a callback.** Only the identity
  row's address follows the provider. The login address is also where
  password-reset mail goes, and a compromised provider account must not be able
  to redirect it.
- **Two concurrent first sign-ins** with one linkable address can both find no
  account; the second hits `uniq_user_email` and gets a retryable `500`, as the
  registration form does in the same race.
```

- [ ] **Step 2: `docs/oauth-sign-in.md` §4.2 gains two subsections**

After the paragraph that ends §4.2:

```markdown
replaces the binding the pending code needs, and the pending exchange fails with
`invalid_token`. Starting again works.
```
and before the `### 4.3` heading, insert (one blank line before and after):
```markdown
#### The login code

The code in the callback's redirect is 64 hex characters from
`random_bytes(32)`. It expires 30 seconds after issue — a read never extends the
window, or a code captured from a log would live as long as something kept
touching it — and it dies on first use. The cache holds the user id, not a JWT:
the token is minted at the exchange, so its `iat` is the moment the session
began, which is what revoking tokens on a password change compares against.

Issuing a code stores a digest of the flow cookie the callback authenticated,
and the exchange compares the cookie it receives against that digest with
`hash_equals`. The binding reuses the flow cookie rather than minting a second
secret, so there is one cookie name, one set of attributes and one lifetime to
keep in step.

The account-status gate runs at the exchange, not at the callback: a
`pending_approval` or `suspended` user still receives a login code, and the
exchange answers with the `403` of section 7.4, which says why, instead of a
redirect that could only say "something went wrong".

#### Storage and the accepted race

Neither store keeps a state, a login code or a flow cookie in readable form.
The cache key is a SHA-256 digest of the state or the code, and the binding is a
digest of the cookie: while a flow is live each of them is a bearer credential,
and on shared hosting the cache pool is a directory of files this application
does not own exclusively, so a directory listing must not be a list of usable
values. A plain SHA-256 is enough — no salt, no work factor — because every
input is 32 bytes from `random_bytes()`, with no guessable preimage to protect.
The cookie's value is minted by the server when the flow starts and never
accepted from the caller, or an attacker could pin the binding to a value they
already know.

Both stores delete an entry before validating it, so a failed check burns the
state or the code instead of leaving it open to another guess. Single use is
still best effort under concurrency: PSR-6 has no compare-and-swap, and
`deleteItem()` reports success whether or not the key existed, so two requests
arriving together can both read the entry.

- Two callbacks carrying one state both spend the same authorization code at the
  provider, which accepts it once. The race costs a round trip and cannot
  produce two sessions.
- Two exchanges carrying one login code both get a JWT for the same user. Both
  racers already held the unguessable code, the second token is worth no more
  than the first and expires on the same schedule, and nothing crosses a user
  boundary.

A lock on every callback and exchange would close the window at a real
per-request cost on shared hosting, against no threat. The race is accepted, not
overlooked.
```

and before the `### 4.4` heading, insert (one blank line before and after):
```markdown
#### Why a hand-written listener

`CorsListener` implements this policy in one class instead of using
`nelmio/cors-bundle`. The bundle suits several client origins, per-path rules or
wildcards; this API has exactly one origin, known at deployment. The bundle's
headline options — `allow_origin: ['*']` and regex patterns — are precisely the
mistakes that matter here, each one line away and caught by no test, while a
listener with no wildcard to reach for shows the whole policy at once. Revisit
this if a second origin ever becomes legitimate.

Three details of the listener are load-bearing:

- It writes the **configured** origin into `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, never
  the request's `Origin` header. The two are equal whenever anything is emitted,
  but reflecting the request's origin is how a CORS configuration turns into
  "any origin, with credentials".
- An `APP_FRONTEND_URL` that does not parse as an absolute URL turns CORS off
  entirely. A misconfiguration must break the SPA loudly, not widen who may call
  the API with cookies attached.
- It answers an allowed preflight ahead of the router and the firewall
  (priority 250), because a preflight carries no cookie and no `Authorization`
  header and would otherwise draw a `405` or a `401`. A preflight from any other
  origin falls through to the router, so the listener never turns an unknown URL
  into a `204`. Every response carries `Vary: Origin`, allowed or not, so a
  shared cache cannot serve one origin's answer to another.
```

```markdown
### The ID-token trust boundary

This application does not verify the signature of the ID tokens it accepts,
and that is deliberate. OpenID Connect Core §3.1.3.7 item 6 allows it in one
case only:

> If the ID Token is received via direct communication between the Client and
> the Token Endpoint (which it is in this flow), the TLS server validation MAY be
> used to validate the issuer in place of checking the token signature.

Read narrowly, the carve-out vouches only for who issued the token, and only for
a token pulled straight off the token endpoint over TLS this application
validated. It is not a general permission to skip signatures. Three classes keep
the precondition true, and `OidcBoundaryTest` fails the build if one of them
loosens:

- **`TokenEndpoint`** makes the call. Its URL is a constant of the provider
  class, so no claim, header or request parameter can nominate the authority
  that vouches for a token. A non-`https` URL is refused before any request;
  `verify_peer` and `verify_host` are restated at the call site so a
  `framework.http_client.default_options` edit elsewhere cannot withdraw them;
  and `max_redirects` is 0, because a followed redirect would mean the bytes came
  from a host other than the pinned one. The class is `final`, and it is the
  only place that constructs an `IdTokenModel`.
- **`IdTokenModel`** is that precondition as a type. It parses nothing; it
  exists so that "where did this token come from" is checked at every call site
  instead of remembered.
- **`IdTokenVerifier`** accepts only an `IdTokenModel`, never a string, and
  checks everything TLS says nothing about: `iss`, `aud`, `azp`, `exp` (with 60
  seconds of clock skew), `nonce` and `sub`. Every check throws the same
  `OAuthFailedException`; only its log detail differs, so a caller cannot tell
  "no such client" from "expired token".

Neither the type nor the test stops someone deliberately writing
`new IdTokenModel($jwt)` around a token from elsewhere. Apple's `form_post`
callback carries exactly such a token in its body. It did not come from the
token endpoint, so the carve-out does not cover it: reading it would need JWKS
signature verification this codebase does not implement, and wrapping it in an
`IdTokenModel` to reuse the verifier would skip the only check standing behind
that channel. The callback reads only the `code`.

Rules inside the verifier that look as if they could be relaxed, and must not
be:

- **`azp`.** Item 5 is enforced: a present `azp` must name this client. Item 4's
  companion SHOULD — require `azp` when `aud` has several values — is
  deliberately not: it identifies the presenter when several parties could
  present a token, and here only this application ever can, from a hard-coded
  endpoint with its own client secret. Enforcing it would reject nothing an
  attacker can send, and would break the day a provider adds a second audience.
- **`sub`.** The subject is half of `user_identity`'s unique key and is stored
  byte for byte. An empty subject would put every such user on one row.
  Surrounding whitespace is refused, not trimmed, because `"123"` and `" 123 "`
  would be two rows for one provider account. C0 control characters are refused
  because a NUL truncates in logs, monitoring and some database drivers, so
  `"1\0a"` and `"1\0b"` may collide downstream. Neither Google (decimal strings)
  nor Apple (opaque tokens) sends anything these rules reject.
- **`email_verified`.** Only a JSON `true` (Google) or the string `"true"`
  (Apple) counts. `"TRUE"` is not case-folded and nothing is cast —
  `(bool) "false"` is `true`. The two mistakes are not symmetric: reading a
  verified address as unverified turns an account link into a new signup, while
  reading an unverified one as verified hands an existing account to whoever
  typed the address.
- **`nonce`.** An empty expected nonce would match a token carrying an empty
  one. `AbstractOidcProvider::exchangeCode()` refuses it before the token call,
  so a broken caller does not burn a single-use code, and the verifier refuses
  it again.
```

**`src/Service/OAuth/LoginCodeStore.php`** (lines 13–71) — **Shorten + move to docs.** The tree's longest block (scope worked example 1). "and used to be" is history and goes; the attack narrative is already §4.2's text; the lifetime, the `iat` reason and the race analysis move to `#the-login-code` and `#storage-and-the-accepted-race`. The binding and the one-answer rule stay as the security warning.

Before:
```php
/**
 * The handover between the provider callback and the SPA.
 *
 * The callback finishes holding an authenticated user but must answer with a
 * redirect — and a JWT in that query string would land in browser history,
 * `Referer` headers, and every proxy log in between. So the redirect carries
 * a code instead: worthless after 30 seconds or after one use, and the SPA
 * POSTs it back for the real token. 30 seconds is generous for "browser
 * follows a redirect, SPA boots" and short enough that a code captured from
 * a log is almost always dead on arrival. The window runs from issue and is
 * never extended by a read; refreshing on access would let a leaked code
 * live indefinitely while something kept touching it.
 *
 * The stored value is a user id, not a JWT: minting the token at exchange
 * time means its `iat` reflects when the session began, which matters
 * because password changes revoke tokens by comparing `iat` against
 * User::$passwordChangedAt.
 *
 * ## The code is NOT a bearer value, and used to be
 *
 * A short life and single use bound how long a leaked code was worth
 * stealing, not who could spend one — a different property, exactly as
 * `state` proving "this server started a flow" differs from "this browser
 * started it" (see OAuthStateStore).
 *
 * The attack the short window did not close: an attacker completes a genuine
 * sign-in in their own browser — forced by OAuthStateStore's binding — then
 * withholds the code. Inside its 30 seconds they point a victim at
 * `<frontend>/auth/callback?code=X`; the SPA exchanges on landing with no
 * user gesture, and the victim's browser ends up holding the ATTACKER's JWT,
 * landing every feed and article in the attacker's account. Thirty seconds
 * is ample, and it scripts.
 *
 * So the code carries the same browser binding the flow does. issue() stores
 * only the digest of the flow token the callback authenticated; consume()
 * requires the matching token back and compares with hash_equals. A missing
 * or wrong binding is null, indistinguishable from unknown, spent or
 * expired — telling them apart would confirm a captured code was live. The
 * binding is the flow cookie the browser already holds, not a second
 * secret, so there is one cookie name, one set of attributes, one lifetime
 * to keep in sync. See OAuthController::FLOW_COOKIE.
 *
 * SINGLE USE IS BEST-EFFORT UNDER CONCURRENCY — same caveat as
 * OAuthStateStore, same reason. consume() deletes before validating, so an
 * expired entry cannot be retried, but redemption is not atomic: PSR-6 has
 * no compare-and-swap, and `deleteItem()` returns true whether or not the
 * key existed. Two exchanges arriving together can both see `isHit()`, both
 * delete, and both get the same user id — the ordering narrows the window
 * between getItem() and deleteItem() but does not close it. Left unclosed
 * deliberately: the failure mode is one user receiving two JWTs instead of
 * one, and that user was entitled to a JWT. Nothing crosses a user boundary
 * — the code is unguessable and both racers already held it, a second token
 * worth no more than the first, expiring on the same schedule. A lock on
 * every exchange would buy nothing on shared hosting but a round trip.
 *
 * Guarantees: the code is unguessable, stored only as a digest, expires 30
 * seconds after issue regardless of reads, and cannot be redeemed twice in
 * sequence.
 */
```
After:
```php
/**
 * Hands the callback's user to the SPA as a 30-second, single-use code bound to the flow cookie, so no JWT rides in a
 * redirect. A wrong binding must look exactly like an unknown code. The accepted redemption race:
 * docs/oauth-sign-in.md#storage-and-the-accepted-race
 */
```

**`src/Service/OAuth/OAuthStateStore.php`** (lines 15–67) — **Shorten + move to docs.** Two `##` sections. The login-CSRF attack and the `SameSite=None` reasoning are already `docs/oauth-sign-in.md` §4.2 text; the minted-not-accepted rule and the race go to `#storage-and-the-accepted-race`. "Proved by driving the endpoints with an empty cookie jar" is `OAuthFlowTest`'s job.

Before:
```php
/**
 * Holds the per-flow secrets between the redirect to the provider and the
 * provider's callback. Server-side and not in a session, because the API is
 * stateless and issues no session cookie.
 *
 * ## `state` alone is not enough
 *
 * On its own `state` is unguessable, was issued by this server, is destroyed on
 * first use, and expires in ten minutes — which proves only *this server started
 * some flow*, not *this browser started this flow*. The gap is login CSRF: an
 * attacker with a real account scripts start(), keeps `state`, approves at the
 * provider and captures `code` from the final redirect WITHOUT following it (so
 * the state is never burned), then gets a victim to open the callback URL. Both
 * values are genuine and unspent, every check passes, and the victim's browser
 * ends up authenticated AS THE ATTACKER. Proved by driving the endpoints with an
 * empty cookie jar.
 *
 * ## The binding
 *
 * start() also mints a `browserToken`, set as a cookie by the controller, and
 * stores only its DIGEST beside the flow; consume() requires the matching token
 * back and refuses a callback that cannot produce it as though the state were
 * unknown. Only a digest is stored, compared with hash_equals, for the same
 * reason the state is only ever a hashed cache key: while a flow is live the
 * token is a bearer credential, and a readable cache directory must not be a list
 * of usable ones. The token is minted here, not accepted from the caller, or an
 * attacker could pin the binding to a value they already know.
 *
 * **The cookie must be `SameSite=None`, and that is not a weakening.** Apple's
 * callback is a cross-site POST (`response_mode=form_post`), which a `Lax` cookie
 * is not sent on — so `Lax` would fail every Apple sign-in with `invalid_state`.
 * `None` requires `Secure`; the confidentiality `SameSite` would give is supplied
 * instead by the value being unguessable and single-use and by the `__Host-`
 * prefix, which forbids a `Domain` attribute so no other host can write this
 * cookie into the backend's origin. See OAuthController for the attributes.
 *
 * ONE FLOW PER BROWSER AT A TIME. One cookie name, so a second sign-in overwrites
 * the first flow's binding and the abandoned tab fails with `invalid_state`. The
 * alternative — a set of live bindings — lets a stranger calling an
 * unauthenticated endpoint write unboundedly to the browser. Somebody who opened
 * two consent screens just starts again.
 *
 * SINGLE USE IS BEST-EFFORT UNDER CONCURRENCY. consume() deletes the entry before
 * validating it, so a state that fails a check is still burned, but redemption is
 * not atomic: PSR-6 offers no compare-and-swap, so two callbacks arriving
 * together can both see isHit(), both delete, and both get the same
 * OAuthStartStateModel. That is deliberate: both racers then spend the SAME
 * authorization code at the provider, which is single-use there, so the second
 * exchange fails on the provider's authority; the race wastes a round trip,
 * cannot produce two sessions, and never crosses a user boundary. Closing it
 * would mean a lock on every callback — a real per-request cost on shared hosting
 * against no real threat.
 */
```
After:
```php
/**
 * Holds a flow's secrets between the redirect and the callback, server-side because the API has no session. A digest
 * of the flow cookie binds the flow to its browser; a missing or wrong cookie must fail like an unknown state.
 * Storage and the accepted race: docs/oauth-sign-in.md#storage-and-the-accepted-race
 */
```

```php
    /**
     * An account that was registered with this address but never confirmed it.

     * Whoever set that password never proved they can read mail at this

     * password discarded.

     * `pending_approval`, and RegistrationService::requestPasswordReset()
     * returns silently for anything that is not `Active` or `Suspended`, so a
     * reset is possible only AFTER an admin approves. The immediate way in is
     * the identity that just claimed the row signing in again with that
     * provider. Approval first, reset second; nobody is stranded.
     *
     * That does not weaken the wipe: the discarded password belongs to
     * someone who never proved the address, while whoever DID prove it holds
     * a working sign-in the moment approval lands — keeping the password for
     * a recovery path would preserve it for the wrong person. Without this,
     * an attacker could park an unverified registration on any address and
     * wait for its real owner to sign in with Google, at which point the
     * attacker's password would unlock the victim's account. setPasswordHash()

     * so a session the attacker somehow holds dies here too.

     * owner can never reach the account that address names) and strands the
     * common legitimate case, where the abandoned registration is the user's

     * only an unproven address and an unused password.
```

```php
/**
 * Builds the thing Apple calls a "client secret" and everyone else calls a
 * signed assertion.
 *
 * Apple issues no static secret: the relying party signs a short JWT with the
 * ES256 private key downloaded once from the developer portal, and that JWT
 * goes in the `client_secret` field of the token request.
 *
 * Two claims are the reverse of the generic OIDC `private_key_jwt` profile;
 * swapping them yields a token Apple rejects with a bare `invalid_client`:
 *
 * - `iss` is the **team** id, not the client id.
 * - `sub` is the **client** id (the Services ID).
 *
 * `kid` goes in the JOSE header, since a team may have several keys and Apple
 * must know which public half checks the signature.
 *
 * Apple caps the lifetime at six months; ours is one hour, minted per request
 * rather than cached — the signing is one cheap ECDSA op, so caching would buy
 * nothing but a longer-lived credential sitting in a cache file.
 */
```
After:
```php
/**
 * Signs the ES256 JWT Apple takes as a client secret: `iss` is the team id and `sub` the Services ID, the reverse of

 */
```

```php
 * The three-legged sign-in: redirect out, callback in, code for token.
 *
 * The callback NEVER hands the SPA a JWT. It redirects with a one-time

 * in a redirect URL would leak via history, Referer and proxy logs, while the
 * code is worthless after 30 seconds or one use.

 * What the code is bound to, which failures are indistinguishable, and where
 * the account-status gate sits is one rule set spanning both legs; it lives in
 * {@see OAuthSignIn}. Left here is the HTTP around it — reading, setting and
 * clearing the binding cookie, and choosing redirect vs problem+json.

 * `exchange` too, so the literal routes are declared FIRST (Symfony matches in
 * declaration order). Verified with `php bin/console router:match`:
 *
 *   /api/auth/oauth/providers        GET      -> api_auth_oauth_providers
 *   /api/auth/oauth/exchange         POST     -> api_auth_oauth_exchange
 *   /api/auth/oauth/google           GET      -> api_auth_oauth_start
 *   /api/auth/oauth/google/callback  GET|POST -> api_auth_oauth_callback

 */
```

```php
 * The three-legged sign-in's HTTP: redirect out, callback in, code for token. Route order is load-bearing: the
```

**`src/EventListener/CorsListener.php`** (lines 16–54) — **Shorten + move to docs.** Scope worked example 3. The one security property stays; the nelmio rationale moves to `#why-a-hand-written-listener`; the same-origin and cross-origin-not-cross-site paragraphs are already docs §4.3 text.

Before:
```php
/**
 * Lets the SPA's origin call this API, WITH cookies.
 *
 * The credentialed part is why this exists: `POST /api/auth/oauth/exchange` needs
 * the `__Host-oauth_flow` cookie to prove the browser exchanging a login code is
 * the one that earned it (see OAuthController, LoginCodeStore). The SPA sends it
 * with `credentials: 'include'`, and a browser attaches cookies cross-origin only
 * when the response says `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, refusing
 * outright if the allowed origin is `*`.
 *
 * So the allowed origin is a single exact string derived from APP_FRONTEND_URL,
 * and the response echoes THAT string, never the request's `Origin` header. The
 * two are equal whenever anything is emitted, so the distinction looks pedantic —
 * it is not: reflecting the request's own origin is how a CORS config becomes
 * "allow anybody with credentials", and this one can't express that mistake.
 *
 * ## Why a listener and not nelmio/cors-bundle
 *
 * The bundle suits several client origins, per-path rules or wildcards; this API
 * has exactly one, known at deploy time. Its headline options —
 * `allow_origin: ['*']` and regex patterns — are precisely the mistakes that
 * matter here, each a one-line edit away and caught by no test. Forty lines with
 * no wildcard to reach for is the smaller surface, on a showcase repo where the
 * reader should see the whole policy at once. Revisit if a second origin becomes
 * legitimate.
 *
 * ## Same-origin deployments
 *
 * Production likely runs SPA and API on ONE origin, where the browser applies no
 * CORS; nothing here breaks that — a same-origin GET sends no `Origin` and gets
 * no headers back, a same-origin POST sends one, matches, and gets headers the
 * browser ignores. The policy is inert there, not load-bearing.
 *
 * Cross-ORIGIN is not cross-SITE: local dev runs the SPA on
 * `http://localhost:4200` and the API on `http://localhost:8000` — different
 * origins (this listener is required) but the same site, since ports aren't part
 * of a site. The flow cookie's `SameSite=None` is for Apple's cross-site callback
 * POST, not for local dev, which would work without it.
 */
```
After:
```php
/**
 * Allows the one configured frontend origin, with credentials, for the OAuth exchange's flow cookie. It echoes the
 * configured string, never the request's Origin: reflecting that would allow any origin with credentials.
 * Why a listener and not a bundle: docs/oauth-sign-in.md#why-a-hand-written-listener
 */
```

**`src/EventListener/InsecureProductionConfigGuardListener.php`** (lines 12–39) — **Shorten + move to docs.** The issue lists this block as stale: `MaintenanceController::isAuthorized()` no longer exists (the empty-token stance is `MaintenanceTokenGuard`'s, now named in the docs).  * Refuses to serve production traffic while a fail-open placeholder is still in

```php
 * that looks healthy indefinitely:
 *
 * ALTCHA_HMAC_KEY ships as a known string in a PUBLIC repository, and the key
 * is the ONLY thing making a challenge unforgeable: anyone holding it forges a
 * valid solution in one hash instead of ~150k, making /register and
 * /password-reset-request's proof-of-work free while they still answer 200.
 * That default fails OPEN; this guard makes it fail closed, the stance
 * App\Controller\MaintenanceController::isAuthorized() already takes on an

 *

 * `cache:warmup` in prod before the `current` symlink flips, so those hooks
 * would abort warmup on a misconfigured environment and take the whole deploy
 * down. kernel.request is safe because secrets need not exist at BUILD time: a
 * host injecting ALTCHA_HMAC_KEY per-request (Apache SetEnv, php-fpm pool
 * directive) sees only the .env default during warmup but the true value by
 * request time. Warmup, migrations and console commands are untouched.
 *
 * The throw surfaces as a 500, deliberately: the operator's message goes to the
 * log (ProblemCatalog suppresses exception messages outside debug), so
 * the client learns nothing while the log names the variable to set. Refusing
```

After:

```php
 * Refuses every production request while ALTCHA_HMAC_KEY still holds the public placeholder from .env, which makes

 */
```
